source: Create a Roblox multiplayer game called Disaster Factory where players become engineers in a factory that designs ridiculous disasters. Each round, players collect resources and earn a budget to build a disaster course using hazards like lava, spinning blades, collapsing bridges, giant boulders, tornadoes, lightning, lasers, explosions, giant rolling objects, and swinging wrecking balls. After building, waves of funny NPCs attempt to reach the exit while players watch the chaos unfold. Players earn money based on how creative, entertaining, and difficult their disaster course is, then unlock new hazards, factory upgrades, themes, and cosmetic effects. Use bright, cartoony visuals with exaggerated physics, satisfying chain reactions, humorous ragdolls, dramatic sound effects, and zero realistic gore. Include multiplayer leaderboards, replay cameras, random challenge modifiers, and endless progression encouraging players to create increasingly creative disaster machines.

image_prompt.text: Flat structural zones framing both sides of the course where players place their hazards, sized for the budget a round earns
A narrowing in the course where the NPC wave bunches up and a well-placed hazard pays off
Collapsing bridges and breakable structures along the route that the hazards bring down
The exit gate at the end of the course that the NPC waves are trying to reach
a bright cartoony factory shell around the course - conveyor belts, oversized machinery, control panels
hazard fixtures placed along the course: lava pits, spinning blades, giant boulders, tornado generators, lightning rods, lasers, explosion charges, rolling objects and swinging wrecking balls

layout_placement.text: The mouth of the course where each wave of NPCs enters
The exit as the end-of-track structure the run is scored against
Resource collection sites players gather from between rounds to earn their build budget

notes: The tower-defense track is inverted here: the player places the hazards and the NPCs are the ones trying to survive the lane, so the end-of-track structure is the NPCs' goal rather than the player's health pool.

Most of the course is built by players at runtime. The generated layout is the empty track, the build zones and the factory shell - not the hazards themselves, which are listed only so the build zones are sized to hold them.
Scoring on creativity and entertainment value, hazard unlocks, replay cameras and challenge modifiers are all outside the layout job.

open_questions.ask: How long is a disaster course - a short room-sized gauntlet, or a long winding track that takes an NPC a minute to walk?
Is the course one fixed track everyone decorates, or does each player get their own plot to lay out from scratch?
Does a round end when the wave is exhausted, when the budget runs out, or on a timer?

answers.ask: How long is a disaster course - a short room-sized gauntlet, or a long winding track that takes an NPC a minute to walk?
answers.answer: Use a short room-sized gauntlet; NPCs should reach the exit quickly so rounds stay fast and the chaos is easy to watch.

answers.ask: Is the course one fixed track everyone decorates, or does each player get their own plot to lay out from scratch?
answers.answer: Each player gets their own small plot to lay out from scratch, so everyone can build and score their own disaster machine during the same round.

answers.ask: Does a round end when the wave is exhausted, when the budget runs out, or on a timer?
answers.answer: The build phase uses a timer, then the round ends once the NPC wave is exhausted or has reached the exit.
